headline: Core outlook raised as merger pauses forward guidance
summary_short: Diluted EPS fell 41% y/y to $1.11 on a tough prior-year gain-on-sale comp, while Core FFO per share rose 1.4% to $2.86, beating outlook. Same Store outlook was raised, but EPS/FFO/Core FFO guidance was suspended pending the Equity Residential merger.
summary_long: Core FFO per share of $2.86 beat the April outlook's $2.77 midpoint, driven by favorable Same Store revenue (+$0.03/share) and lower operating expense (-$0.06/share) versus plan. GAAP EPS fell 41% y/y to $1.11 because Q2 2025 included a $99.5M gain on sale of previously depreciated real estate that didn't repeat. Same Store residential NOI rose 1.0% y/y on 1.6% revenue growth partly offset by 2.9% expense growth. The company repaid $475M of unsecured notes at par, ended the quarter with $80.7M cash, and reported Net Debt-to-Core EBITDAre of 4.6x. Full-year Same Store revenue and NOI outlook was raised; EPS, FFO and Core FFO guidance was suspended pending the Equity Residential merger.
confidence_notes: REGENERATED — this summary force-overwrites any prior run per operator instruction (fresh recompute from the same primary source, not a data correction). All EPS/NOI/net-income/debt/equity KPI values are SEC-verbatim from the shard (rederive-sec-xbrl) and were cross-checked line-by-line against this press release's own reconciliation tables (EBITDA, FFO, NOI, Net Debt) — all matched exactly. The y/y declines in EPS, net income, EBITDA and pretax income are a base-effect artifact of a large $99.5M prior-year (Q2 2025) gain on sale of previously depreciated real estate, not an operating deterioration — see drivers. The XBRL LongTermDebt tag ($9,024.8M) runs about $54M below the company's own 'total debt principal' figure ($9,079.1M) used in its Net Debt-to-Core EBITDAre calc, likely a scope difference (e.g. commercial paper treatment), not an error. AvalonBay did not hold an earnings call this quarter given the pending Equity Residential merger.

drivers.explanation: Company's own per-share bridge: a $0.69 swing from real estate gains/depreciation (Q2 2025 had a large gain on sale) plus $0.10 of Core FFO adjustments, partly offset by +$0.08 development NOI and +$0.03 same-store NOI.
Same base effect as EPS: the FFO reconciliation table shows Q2 2025 net income included a $99.5M gain on sale of previously depreciated real estate that isn't repeated in Q2 2026.
EBITDA (unlike EBITDAre) doesn't back out gains on sale, so the y/y decline mechanically reflects the same ~$99.5M prior-year gain that also drove the EPS and net income declines.
Same Store residential revenue rose 1.6% y/y on higher rents; COO attributed the improved outlook to "a healthier demand environment, easing new supply, and disciplined execution."
Company repaid $475M principal of its 2.95% coupon unsecured notes at par upon maturity during the quarter.
Equity rose as the company settled outstanding equity forward contracts, issuing 2.76M shares at $220.08 for $607.4M of proceeds.
Y/y share count fell as the company repurchased 1,130,336 shares YTD at an average $175.59, partly offset by 2.76M forward shares issued in Q2.

CEO called Q2 "strong, exceeding expectations"; COO cited demand, easing supply, and execution behind the raised Same Store outlook, while EPS/FFO/Core FFO guidance was suspended given the pending Equity Residential merger.
